name: A Global Living Lab: Light DAO's Next International Gathering
description:
Members of Light DAO's leadership recently participated in Edge Esmeralda and came away feeling it was one of the most impressive, inspiring and transformative business gatherings we had ever experienced - because it was not a conference, retreat or summit.

It was a Society Incubator - an extraordinary integration of worlds that are rarely found in one place.

In a single day, you might:

 Begin the morning with a tea ceremony, breathwork or yoga

 Move into a talk with brilliant researchers, founders and investors on frontier science and emerging technology

 Spend a few hours building software, testing experimental health wearables, collaborating in a maker space, or creating in a media lab

 Head into nature, join a wellness session, or get absorbed in a discussion on the latest in AI agents, fintech or longevity

 Continue the conversations over dinner late into the evening - or end the night with music, ecstatic dance or a calming sound bath

 For families, dedicated programs for kids and teens, starting at age 4, offer opportunities to play, learn, create and build within their own community

 Alongside all of this are deep conversations about consciousness, philosophy, society and human flourishing

It felt like stepping into a living laboratory for the future - a temporary village designed to explore and experiment with how we might live, work, learn, build and thrive differently.

It offered a glimpse of what the world could look like when innovation, human flourishing and community are developed together.

## This is Edge City.

Edge Cities are 3-4-week Living Labs and Society Incubators - international popup villages where frontier technology, science, entrepreneurship, consciousness, culture, art, well-being and community are not separate tracks, but part of one shared environment.

Edge Cities have already taken place in Patagonia, Chiang Mai, Cape Town and Esmeralda, two hours north of San Francisco.

Edge Esmeralda - June 2026

- 850 residents from 60+ countries
- Nearly 300 stayed for the full month
- 800+ sessions and experiments
- Families came with 48 kids

What made it so extraordinary was being surrounded by brilliant, conscious innovators genuinely committed to advancing humanity - with enough time together for real relationships, collaborations and radical ideas to develop.

[www.EdgeEsmeralda.com](https://www.EdgeEsmeralda.com)

That experience convinced us that Edge City offers something unusually valuable for the Light DAO community.

So this October, we're taking our community to the next Edge City.

## The Next Edge City: Goa, India

October 11 - November 1, 2026

We're taking our community to Edge India in Goa - a three-week Living Lab and Society Incubator with hundreds of participants, approximately 65% coming from outside India.

Light DAO will have our own RESIDENCY within the larger Edge India community, so our members can take part in the full Edge experience while also connecting more intimately with our own community.

## A Living Lab Created by Its Community

One of the things that make Edge Cities especially unique and powerful is their unconference-style format. Much of the experience is created by the participants themselves - through the talks, demos, experiments and working groups they lead around the ideas and projects they care most about.

Light DAO will also host more intimate gatherings within our own Residency, led by our guests.

Once registered, Light DAO Owner Members are welcome to contact us with ideas you might like to lead or contribute to. We can't guarantee a place in either the Light DAO or Edge programming, but we'd love to hear what you are most excited to share.

That participatory spirit is part of what makes Edge a true Living Lab: the community does not simply attend the experience - it helps create it.

## A Special Light DAO + SingularityNET Residency

We're delighted to be partnering with SingularityNET for a 3-week Light DAO + SingularityNET Residency at Edge India. This is the first collaboration of its kind we've run with the SingularityNET team.

Everyone racing toward AGI is making the same bet: that a bigger model gets there. SingularityNET is not.

Led by Dr. Ben Goertzel, who launched the term and concept of Artificial General Intelligence, the team scales Beneficial General Intelligence on Hyperon, a cognitive architecture with two decades of research behind it. It holds knowledge, goals and decisions in a form you can inspect, shows its reasoning, and runs under explicit permissions - which is what makes it deployable inside real institutions.

The residency puts you in the room with the people building it. Talks, working sessions and open build time for developers, founders, researchers, investors, and anyone serious about AGI, ASI and beneficial technology.

Bring what you are already building. Leave with something concrete: a technical integration, a partnership, an investment conversation, or a prototype you put together on-site at Edge India.

## Why Join the Light DAO + SingularityNET Residency?

In addition to the full Edge India experience, our Residency gives you a more intimate community to connect, collaborate and build with throughout your stay, including:

 Light DAO + SingularityNET talks, working sessions and open build time

 More intimate conversations and collaborations within our residency group, particularly with SingularityNET's leadership and tech team.

 Light DAO-organized meals, including opportunities for participants to lead topic conversations

 Optional group outings and shared experiences

 Opportunities for Light DAO Owner Members to propose topics they may want to lead or contribute to

 A shared home base at our beachfront resort

Think of our residency as your home community within the larger Edge India Living Lab.

## What Makes Edge Cities a Unique Living Lab + Society Incubator

Hear Edge Cities co-founder Timour Kosters talk about the multidisciplinary, multigenerational and global vision behind Edge Cities - including its unconference format and experiments.

He shares how the experience stretches people's sense of what is possible, helps them embody that expansion, and activates new collaborations and directions. In 1-3 weeks, many participants accelerate results that might otherwise have taken months or longer.

The Edge experience is designed around focused work, collaboration, wellness, community and time to enjoy Goa.

Your Edge Pass includes the full Edge India experience - programming, coworking, wellness, community gatherings and more.

## Pricing

Edge India Pass

Prices increase weekly

- 2-3 weeks (same price): $1,500-$2,000
- 1 week: $750-$1,000
- Day pass: $150-$200
- Indian citizens: 50% discount

 Our Beachfront 4-Star Resort

[www.RivaResorts.com](https://www.RivaResorts.com)

Our Light DAO + SingularityNET Residency will be based at Edge India's central hotel.

- Private room + breakfast: $100 per room/night
- Lunch + dinner: approximately $30 - 50/day
  Your choice - at the resort or anywhere in Goa

Yes - you get your own private room. At $100/night including breakfast, this is an exceptional value for a beachfront 4-star resort.

If you're coming as a couple, it is the same $100/night including breakfast for 2!

Roommates also the same $100/night!

Lunches, dinners and excursions are paid for individually, giving you the flexibility to join our residency plans, other Edge activities, or your own plans in Goa.

## Joining the Light DAO + SingularityNET Residency

Edge Cities are curated communities with an application and approval process.

Light DAO Owner Members and friends we already know:
Please RSVP here on Luma. You will automatically be approved for Edge India through our Residency.

If you are new to us:
Please RSVP here on Luma and complete the registration questions thoughtfully. Thank you.

Once approved through the Light DAO + SingularityNET Residency, you will not need to complete a separate Edge City application.

Ready to Join?
Choose one of the two ticket options above.
Once approved, we'll send you:

- the direct link to purchase your Edge ticket at the current lowest price
- the resort reservation link

Come experience our collaboration between Edge Cities, SingularityNET and Light DAO - where frontier ideas, deep community and real opportunities to build and collaborate come together in one Living Lab.

You may leave with a partnership, a prototype, a new collaborator, or an entirely new direction you had not imagined before joining this unique Society Incubator.

The program selects 30 residents. Scholarships cover eight nights of accommodation, food and drinks, on-site activities and the closing summit on October 30. Participants choose among the Logos Civic Prize, Logos Sovereignty and Privacy, Zu-Grama d/acc, and a non-builder track for activists, community organizers and artists. Technical work includes privacy-preserving blockchain, decentralized governance, censorship-resistant storage and secure payments. Creatives, designers and testers can also apply.

The schedule includes stand-ups, mentoring, dedicated build time, workshops and demos. Residents present prototypes at the closing summit. The strongest Logos-track prototypes are eligible for milestone-based grant funding. Applicants are asked to install Logos Basecamp, add its blockchain module and note the block height; an existing demo or prototype is helpful but not required.

name: Bitshala BOSS Summit 2026 | Jaipur | 26 Oct - 31 Oct
description:
## Bitshala BOSS (Bitcoin Open-Source Software) Summit 2026 | Jaipur

Join us for 6 days of fun, work, collaboration, and deep learning at the frontiers of Bitcoin open-source software design and development.

## What's happening

Expect a highly collaborative residency with sessions, workshops, demos, open discussions, and hands-on building time.

You'll get to:

- Learn what's happening at the frontiers of Bitcoin OSS development and design
- Meet developers and designers working on active Bitcoin projects
- Connect with product builders and educators taking Bitcoin to more people
- Share demos, prototypes, workshops, and project ideas
- Find collaborators for GitHub repos, Figma files, personal projects, or products
- Spend time with fellow builders through games, sports, bonfires, walks, treks, and sightseeing

Whether you're contributing to open-source software, designing better Bitcoin user experiences, building educational content, or working on a product, BOSS Summit is designed to help you meet the right people and move your work forward.

## Timelines

- Monday, 26 Oct
  - Check-in
  - 16:00 : Welcome & introductions
- Tuesday, 27 Oct - Thursday, 29 Oct (10:00 - 17:00)
  - Sessions, Workshops, Open Slots, Demos, Project discussions and Collaboration time
  - Evenings will include fun games, sports, bonfires, and informal hangouts.
- Friday, 30 Oct - Saturday, 31 Oct
  - Bitmela
- Sunday, 1 Nov
  - Checkout by 11:00 AM

## Who Should Apply

We have limited seats for:

- Bitcoin developers
- Product designers
- UX/UI designers
- Bitcoin educators
- Product builders
- People actively working on Bitcoin projects, tools, content, or education

Seats are sponsored by Bitshala, so please make a strong application to help us understand what you're working on and how you hope to contribute during the residency.

## Bring Your Work

Have an active GitHub repo, a Figma file, a workshop idea, a product prototype, or a personal project?

Bring it along.

BOSS Summit is a place to share work-in-progress, find collaborators, get feedback, jam on ideas, and build alongside others who care deeply about Bitcoin and open-source software.

## Bringing a Family Member or Friend

If you're planning to bring a family member or friend, we'll connect you with the venue provider or Airbnb options.

You can directly pay for their stay and meals with the provider.

## Apply to Get Invited

BOSS Summit has limited invited seats for Bitcoin developers, designers, educators, and builders.

If you're excited to learn, contribute, build, teach, design, or collaborate around Bitcoin open-source software, we'd love to hear from you.

Apply now and tell us what you're building.

For any queries drop a mail to contact@bitshala.org

## Glimpse of Our Last BOSS Summit

Dharmshala - Summer 2026

Catch a glimpse of the energy, collaboration, and moments from our last BOSS Summit in Dharmshala - from deep work sessions and demos to bonfires, games, and community bonding.

Explore [more here: The official BOSS Summit After-Movie and Article](https://x.com/bitshala_org/status/2049831566827008161)

## About Bitshala

[Bitshala](https://bitshala.org/) is a Bitcoin-focused education initiative where we help developers, designers, and curious builders learn by doing. We run cohorts, clubs, workshops, a hackerspace, and community programs that make it easier for people to explore, contribute to, and build on Bitcoin. Our focus is on hands-on learning, proof-of-work, and growing alongside a community of people who care about open technology, design, and the future of money.

If you'd like to explore more, check us out on:

- Discord (Online Community) (https://discord.com/invite/STeQFVEWf9)
- [Cohort registration and fellowship application portal](https://app.bitshala.org/)

- Twitter (Socials and Announcements) (https://x.com/bitshala_org)
- Luma (Events Calendar) (https://luma.com/bitshala)

name: BCNL x VBNL x PwC - CARF & DAC8 Roundtable
description:
The regulatory landscape for digital assets continues to evolve. With CARF and DAC8, crypto businesses and financial institutions face a new set of tax transparency, due diligence, data, and reporting requirements.

Together with PwC Netherlands, BCNL and VBNL are organizing an exclusive and highly interactive session focused entirely on what CARF and DAC8 mean in practice.

Date: 28-10-26
15:30 - 19:00
PwC Netherlands
Limited & curated attendance

## From regulation to implementation

The session will be led by PwC's team of operational tax experts, specializing in areas including FATCA/CRS, CESOP and Digital Services Taxes. The team includes a former OECD member who contributed to the development of CARF, complemented by operational tax professionals with more than 10 years of experience in the financial sector.

Rather than focusing solely on the technical regulation, this session is designed to answer the practical questions:

What does CARF/DAC8 actually mean for your organization? What do you need to prepare? Where are the known pitfalls? And what challenges are other organizations already encountering?

## The 5 Building Blocks of CARF

During the roundtable, PwC will take participants through five key areas:

1. Entity Management
Determining whether your organization falls within the scope of the regulation.

2. Product Analysis
Identifying which products and services are in scope.

3. Due Diligence
Understanding the requirements, how to implement them, and how they align with existing AML/KYC processes.

4. Reporting
What needs to be reported, where and when, which data points are required, and what this means for your organization and systems.

5. Governance Set-up
Establishing the right policies, procedures, responsibilities, and internal governance.

For each building block, we'll connect the regulatory requirements with real-world implementation, known pitfalls, and challenges PwC is seeing across the market.

## An interactive roundtable

This is deliberately a small-scale and interactive session, not a traditional conference.

The core roundtable will last approximately two hours, with plenty of room for discussion, practical cases, and questions from participants. Attendees will also have the opportunity to submit questions and topics in advance, allowing the PwC team to tailor the conversation to the challenges organizations are actually facing.

Following the session, we'll continue with drinks and networking, giving participants the opportunity to exchange experiences and connect with peers.

## Who should attend?

The session is particularly relevant for finance, tax, compliance and operational professionals working at:

Crypto exchanges - Brokers - Payment providers & PSPs - E-money institutions - Market makers - Banks & financial institutions - Other organizations active in or expanding into digital assets

Professionals from traditional financial institutions exploring or expanding their crypto activities are also very welcome.

About PwC Netherlands

PwC Netherlands supports crypto businesses in navigating evolving tax transparency and reporting requirements, including CARF, CESOP, DAC7, and relevant domestic obligations. By combining tax, regulatory, and technology capabilities, PwC helps organizations assess their scope and build the data, systems, processes, and governance required for sustainable compliance.

About BCNL Foundation

BCNL Foundation connects and strengthens the Dutch digital asset ecosystem by bringing together companies, financial institutions, policymakers, investors, and industry professionals through events, education, advocacy, and strategic collaboration.

About NVC (VBNL)
NVC is the Dutch CASP Association, formerly known as VBNL. Founded in 2014, NVC has a long history advocating for the interests of bitcoin- and crypto companies, promoting self-regulation, coordination with stakeholders such as legislators, regulators and law enforcement, and maintaining the highest standards of reputation and integrity. Members are: Bitvavo, MoonPay, Coinmerce, zerohash, Blockrise, BTC Direct, Bitmymoney, Blox, Fiat Republic, Acheron Trading & Finst.

Capacity is limited and registrations will be curated.

If CARF/DAC8 could impact your organization, this is an opportunity to discuss the implications directly with experts and peers before the requirements become part of day-to-day operations.

The blockchain ecosystem deserves a home. A place where the people actually get together to build the future of this industry. The researchers, the founders, the engineers, the policymakers can all be in the same room, have the conversations that matter and leave with something they didn't have when they arrived.

That belief built TBC. And every year it gets a little closer to what we always imagined it could be.

Day 2, Digital Assets Day by Bundesblock: where traditional finance meets the onchain economy.

Day 2 and 3, the Hackathon: 30 hours to build, ship and compete across many partner tracks.

We are TUM Blockchain Club, a student organization that has punched well above its weight since the beginning. Our ambition has always been to host the events that actually matter. The one where a researcher from a leading university sits next to a protocol founder and they realize they've been working on the same problem from different ends. The one where a student attends a talk that changes the direction of their career. The one where something gets built that ends up mattering.

That is what we are creating. Not a conference. A moment the whole ecosystem looks forward to all year.

Come for the talks. Stay for the builders. Leave with something you didn't expect.

description:
## Hong Kong Crypto Compliance & Legal Community Drinks

Join us on Thursday, October 29, from 6pm onwards for a relaxed evening of drinks and conversation with the Hong Kong Crypto Compliance & Legal Community.

This informal meetup is all about bringing together compliance, legal, policy, financial crime and regulatory professionals working across the digital asset ecosystem. It's a chance to connect with peers, exchange ideas, share experiences and build meaningful relationships; and this time you want to add some pre-Halloween vibes lol.

There's no agenda, no panels - just good conversations and a welcoming crowd.

 Expect:

- A friendly and relaxed atmosphere
- Conversations on crypto compliance, legal and regulatory developments
- Opportunities to connect with professionals from across the digital asset ecosystem
- A chance to unwind after work over a glass of wine or a beer

Whether you're working at a crypto company, bank, law firm, regulator or advisory firm, we'd love to have you join us.

Drinks are pay-as-you-go. Come by, bring a colleague, and let's continue growing the Hong Kong Crypto Compliance & Legal Community together.

About the Crypto Compliance & Legal Community

The Crypto Compliance & Legal Community brings together compliance, legal, policy and regulatory professionals from across the digital asset industry.

Our ambition is simple: bring together the right people in the room to have honest conversations, share experiences and build meaningful relationships. Through regular meetups and our global Telegram community of more than 3,300 members, we're building a trusted network for professionals shaping the future of digital assets.

name: Money in Motion: The Future of Cross-Border Payments
description:
The infrastructure powering global payments is undergoing a fundamental shift.

Digital assets, emerging financial technologies, and evolving regulatory frameworks are creating new possibilities for how money moves across borders. As traditional financial systems converge with digital asset infrastructure, new opportunities and challenges are emerging for businesses, financial institutions, and investors.

Beyond the promise of faster and more efficient transactions, important questions remain. How can innovation operate within existing regulatory frameworks? What does it take to build reliable, scalable cross-border payment infrastructure? And where do the most compelling opportunities lie for founders and investors?

LedgerPe Labs and Chambers of Rachana Rautray invite you to Money in Motion, an exclusive industry gathering exploring the intersection of regulation, financial infrastructure, digital assets, and venture capital.

The evening will feature a focused industry discussion followed by an opportunity to connect with fellow founders, investors, and professionals shaping the future of global finance.

## The Conversation

One Panel. Multiple Perspectives.

The discussion will explore four interconnected themes:

Regulation & Compliance

Understanding the evolving regulatory landscape for cross-border payments, with a focus on India-UAE corridors, digital asset frameworks, and the responsibilities of financial intermediaries.

Infrastructure & Execution

Examining the practical challenges of building reliable cross-border payment systems, including liquidity, settlement, banking partnerships, interoperability, and operational resilience.

Investment & Opportunities

Exploring emerging business models, opportunities for innovation, and what makes financial infrastructure companies commercially sustainable, scalable, and attractive to investors.

The Road Ahead

Discussing the future of institutional adoption, the convergence of digital assets and traditional finance, and the next generation of global payment infrastructure.

## Evening Agenda

5:00 PM - 6:00 PM | Panel Discussion & Audience Q&A

A moderated conversation exploring the regulatory, technological, and commercial realities of cross-border payments.

6:00 PM - 7:00 PM | Networking & Refreshments

Continue the conversation over refreshments and connect with founders, investors, fintech executives, and professionals working across financial services and digital assets.

## Event Details

Date: Friday, 30 October 2026
Time: 5:00 PM - 7:00 PM IST
Venue: Spotlight Strategic Partners, Andheri East, Mumbai
Format: Industry Panel & Networking

Community Partner: Spotlight Strategic Partners

An evening bringing together the people building, enabling, and investing in the future of cross-border finance.

Limited seats. Registration is subject to approval.

name: IBW Institutional Forum
description:
Hashed Emergent convenes the IBW Institutional Forum at Fairmont Mumbai on November 1 and 2, 2026. This invitation-only, closed-door forum is a dedicated room within India Blockchain Week Conference, planned for 100 to 120 senior leaders. The format combines keynotes, expert panels and fireside conversations about institutional blockchain adoption.

The intended participants include Indian banks, NBFCs, payments and capital-markets firms, global financial institutions, enterprise technology and tokenization teams, regulators and policy advisers. The organizer seeks C-suite and director-level participants, including heads of digital assets or blockchain, technology and digital officers, payments and settlement leaders, and treasury and capital-markets product heads.

### Discussion areas

- CBDCs and programmable money: conditional disbursements, offline payments and moving the programmable rupee beyond pilots.
- Tokenization and real-world assets: fractional equities, tokenized funds, custody, infrastructure and applicable rules.
- Trade finance and settlement: letters of credit, e-way bills and cross-border settlement on shared systems.
- Capital-markets infrastructure: DLT-based covenant monitoring and regulatory sandbox pilots.
- Institutional DLT: production systems used by enterprise technology providers across Indian institutions.
- AI and blockchain: autonomous agents and verifiable onchain infrastructure.

Discussions follow the Chatham House Rule. Participants may use information from the room without identifying the speaker or their organization.

Attendance requires selection by the programming team. The [delegate application](https://indiablockchainweek.com/institutional-forum/apply) reserves seats for IBW2026 Priority, VIP and Executive VIP pass holders and asks applicants to buy their pass first. The team reviews each application and confirms participation by email. A qualifying pass does not itself secure a forum seat.

The organizer also accepts proposals to speak, partner or sponsor through the forum page. The names displayed as speakers from previous IBW editions are historical examples, not the forum's confirmed 2026 lineup.

name: IBW Future Asset Forum 2026
description:
Hashed Emergent and Mugafi convene Future Asset Forum at Fairmont Mumbai on November 1 and 2, 2026, within India Blockchain Week. The invitation-only forum examines ownership and financing in sports, entertainment and media as AI changes production, localization and distribution. The page lists a 09:00 IST start and describes cross-registration with the Institutional Forum.

### Working program

The organizers plan 18 sessions and have published twelve working titles across four parts:

- Asset value: the financial limits of buying only successful titles; the different underwriting problems of franchises, catalogues and production slates; and the legal and commercial treatment of voice and likeness rights.
- Ownership and financing: debt-based participation, institutional investment in US leagues and Indian franchises, and financial instruments that could support these assets in India.
- Connecting the assets: a live look at disconnected fan datasets, the wider economics of a stadium event, and Indian law concerning provenance.
- Production and demand: AI's effect on production budgets, the business of physical venues and live attendance, and prospective buyers of these assets in 2031.

The proposed discussion format asks each panelist to commit in writing to sharing one previously unpublished figure in the room, off the record. Speaker names are published after the organizers receive written confirmation.

### Participation

Seats are allocated by participant category rather than sold as public tickets. The intended allocation is 40% rights holders and media operators, 20% AI and technology companies, 20% capital providers and family offices, 10% distribution and platforms, and 10% policy, legal and press participants. These are the organizers' allocation targets.

The planned participants include studio principals, franchise and league heads, catalogue owners, personality-rights lawyers, streaming and exhibition operators, venue and live-event businesses, ticketing and payments teams, fan-data platforms, AI companies, structured-finance specialists, insurers and institutional capital providers.

The [forum page](https://indiablockchainweek.com/future-asset-forum#apply) links applications for partners, sponsors and speakers. The stated process is an application followed by a 30-minute conversation about objectives and category fit, then a tailored proposal within a week. Partnership formats include keynote participation, panels or masterclasses, roundtables or workshops, and demonstrations on the partner floor; availability and pricing are by inquiry.

name: Touch Grass, Not Contracts | Security Researchers' Walk
description:
You can spend four days collecting conference contacts - or 45 minutes actually getting to know a few security people.

A free 45-minute waterfront walk. No stage, no microphone, no forced networking. Come on your own - it's normal here.

## Who is this for?

Auditors, bug hunters, smart-contract security researchers, protocol engineers, and security-curious Devcon ticket holders. Everyone is welcome regardless of gender or experience.

## Why come?

Find fellow researchers, compare real lessons from hacks and audits, and start conversations that aren't another panel Q&A.

Conversation starter (optional): What's one security red flag you wish every DeFi user understood?

## Meet-up details

- Date: Sunday, 1 November 2026
- Walk: 7:00-7:45 AM IST. Arrive by 6:50 AM so you can find the group before we start.
- Mapped meeting landmark: Chhatrapati Shivaji Maharaj Monument, 1 Juhu Tara Road, Juhu, Mumbai 400049. Use the map pin on this event page, not the conference venue.
- Exact entrance and route: The host will confirm the precise side of the landmark and safe public pedestrian path in a Luma update before the event. This is a proposed meeting area, not an inspected route yet.
- Pace: Easy walking for 45 minutes; a gentle jog is optional. No fitness requirements.
- Bring: Drinking water, comfortable shoes, a charged phone and curiosity.

## Tickets and joining

This walk is FREE and registration is open without a fixed attendance cap. A valid Devcon 8 ticket is required to participate. The RSVP does not provide a Devcon ticket. Confirm that you hold one in the sign-up form; never upload your QR code or wallet secrets.

Please be considerate: Respect pedestrians, other attendees and different paces; no unsolicited pitches. We'll stay in public pedestrian areas and avoid traffic lanes and unsafe shoreline sections. If weather, access or route checks require a change, registered guests will receive updated joining details in Luma.

Hosted independently by Veerendra Vamshi (Proof of Audits). Not an official Devcon or Ethereum Foundation event.

name: DeFi Security Summit 2026
description:
The fifth DeFi Security Summit takes place at Courtyard by Marriott Mumbai International Airport on November 1 and 2, 2026, from 10:00 to 18:00 IST each day. It is intended for security researchers, auditors, protocol builders and the wider DeFi community. The venue address is CTS 215, Andheri-Kurla Road, opposite Carnival Cinemas, Andheri East, Mumbai, Maharashtra 400093.

The organizer has published a [2026 talk directory](https://defisecuritysummit.org/2026/agenda), although its Luma description still says speakers and program details are forthcoming. The directory identifies the following talks with the November 1 and 2 Marriott summit. Individual session times and rooms remain to be assigned.

### Published talks

- Hudson Jameson, head of Web3 at CertiK, revisits the 2017 Parity multisig hacks.
- Steffen Kux, co-founder and co-CEO of corpus.core, discusses trustless transaction analysis before Ethereum wallet signatures.
- Dmytro Matviiv, CEO of HackenProof, examines changes in crowdsourced security, including Code4rena and Hats Finance.
- Natalia Klaus, verification engineer at Runtime Verification, covers a pipeline from production Rust to Lean 4 proofs using AI provers.
- 0xa5df, senior security researcher at Certora, approaches auditing as system risk management.
- Kirk Baird, executive director of Sigma Prime, examines single points of failure in blockchain security.
- Shebin John, senior research engineer at Safe Research, presents a deny-by-default policy engine for Safe.
- Rahul Saxena, founder of Bluethroat Labs, addresses attestation gaps in private AI and TEE-backed DeFi.
- Paul Clemson, audit engineer at Quantstamp, examines collateral flows when auditing Polymarket V2.
- Kalp Shah, smart contract auditor at QuillAudits, discusses circuit-level exploits in DeFi.
- Jacob Czepluch covers Core Solidity.
- Michael Lewellen, head of solutions engineering at Turnkey, examines recovery mechanisms as an attack surface.
- Don Josey, founder of Glossifi, asks how financial incentives affect security judgment.
- Ofir Eliasi, CTO of Lava Foundation, covers security during live Cosmos-to-EVM migrations and the risks of unaudited RPC infrastructure.
- Lokesh Joshi, blockchain and AI engineer, discusses autonomous defense for DeFi.
- Mohamad Mansouri, Web3 security researcher at Dedaub, evaluates AI auditing against real smart-contract audits.
- Victor Okafor, security researcher at QuillAudits, considers quantum threats beyond post-quantum signatures.
- George Loukovitis, senior engineer at Dedaub, combines deterministic analysis and language models to detect unsafe ERC-20 behavior.
- Akand Sitra of Hypernative covers real-time Web3 security monitoring.
- Gerard Persoon, security researcher at Cantina, examines conversion between EVM bytecode and Solidity.
- Anu Adeleke of QuillAudits presents a session on vulnerable Daml code.
- Nemveer, senior security researcher at Certora, discusses ecosystem-specific security lessons from auditing NEAR.
- Raj Kumar, security researcher at Certora, and senior threat researcher Sabanaku77 examine monitoring internals, chain data and incident response.
- Henri Binsztok, co-founder and CEO of OKcontract Labs, examines how a multisig can approve an unintended transaction.
- Uri Kirstein, product manager for Fordefi's blockchain team, discusses information missing from Safe transaction decoders.
- Igor Gulamov, co-founder of SavantChat, applies AI auditing to consensus, mempools and peer-to-peer systems.
- Viraz Malhotra, senior blockchain engineer and security researcher, introduces a methodology for AI-assisted auditing.
- Nicolas Garcia, security researcher at OpenZeppelin, discusses when to deploy an AI auditor and disclose its findings.
- Jochen Hoenicke, formal verification researcher at Certora, examines a self-liquidation issue in Morpho Midnight involving a callback window.
- Josselin Feist, security researcher at Aave Labs, addresses security leadership.
- Jeff Fei, security researcher at Ant International, presents SOAC and zero-trust smart-contract permission governance.
- Jork Leonhardt, co-founder of Corpus Core GmbH, covers RPC trust failures affecting builders and monitoring tools.
- Daniel Monzón, offensive security engineer at Halborn, discusses Web3 red-teaming methods.
- Robert Reith, CEO and co-founder of Accretion and hackhack, examines bugs missed by AI tools.
- Abhimanyu Nag, engineering manager at Muchlearning/Canvas, models cryptoeconomic attacks and adversaries in DeFi.
- Andy M. Lee, founder and CEO of Mamori, examines what fuzzing establishes about smart-contract security.
- Magnus Woodgate, lead security engineer at Asymmetric Research, has two listed talks on post-quantum signatures, stateful risks and Ethereum account security.
- Joaquin Pereyra, lead security engineer at Coinspect, examines the discovery of and response to the Ill Bloom wallet-generation flaw.
- Sumanjeet, maintainer of py-libp2p and unified-testing, shares security and operational lessons from py-libp2p and Py-IPFS-lite.
- Julia Hardy, co-founder and head of investigations at zeroShadow, discusses using money-laundering intelligence to contain active exploits.
- Christopher von Hessert, head of security at Polygon Labs, presents "Never Send a Human to Do a Machine's Job."
- Clément Moller, smart contract engineer at Origin Protocol, covers DeFi liveness testing with stateful invariants and replacing a staking oracle with beacon-chain proofs.
- Davit Kobakhidze of Consensys Diligence discusses AI security challenges looking ahead to 2027.
- Christian Vari, head of audit operations at Oak Security, presents an adversarial methodology for AI audits and a four-year study comparing audit findings with exploits.
- Bernardo Codesido, head of security at RootstockLabs, discusses building a lasting crypto security team.
- Nikita Belenkov, security engineer at Anza, examines running an audit competition.
- Doris Benda, blockchain security engineer and auditor at ChainSecurity, covers dirty bits in Solidity.
- Hrishikesh Bhat of Cantina examines the development of crowdsourced security beyond bounties.
- Sofia Bobadilla, PhD student at KTH Royal Institute of Technology, discusses smart-contract invariants as a defense against attacks.
- Zakaryae Boudi, founder of Tokenfrastructure Group, examines vulnerabilities created by the interaction of otherwise correct contracts.
- Petar Calic, protocol lead at Spectra, covers the opportunities and pitfalls of formal verification with AI.
- Lilian Cariou, security and formal-verification researcher at Certora, examines Aave V4's hub-and-spoke architecture.

description:

The event brings together digital-rights advocates, free and open-source software contributors, cryptographers, developers, researchers, artists and legal practitioners. Its 2026 theme, The Ancestral Fork, examines inherited technological and social assumptions about privacy and digital autonomy, with participation from the Global South.

The 2026 program themes cover open-source AI and shared AI resources; responses to internet censorship using tools such as mesh networks and cross-border digital currencies; community-led interactive experiences; and privacy and data-protection questions around Aadhaar, UPI and DigiLocker. Other themes address accessible privacy for inexpensive phones and nontechnical users, and sustainable funding for privacy technology and free software.

The speaker announcement also identifies confidential computation, encrypted mempools, secure messaging, privacy-preserving identity, self-hosted nodes, stealth-address wallets, Kohaku wallet privacy and alternatives to centralized collaboration software as areas of work represented at the event. ### Discussion topics

- Moving funds, bonds and real-estate structures onchain, including ERC-3643, ERC-4626 vaults, NAV oracles, transfer restrictions and compliance controls.
- Stablecoins as payment infrastructure, including reserve attestations, mint and burn controls, blacklisting, freezing and issuer exploits.

The dinner follows the Chatham House Rule and excludes recording, press and slide presentations. Participants may use information from the discussion without identifying its source.

name: Devcon 2026
description:
The Ethereum Foundation hosts Devcon 8 at Jio World Centre in Mumbai's Bandra Kurla Complex from November 3 to 6, 2026. The four-day conference is for developers, researchers, open-source contributors, designers, artists and community organizers working on Ethereum and decentralized systems. Curious beginners are welcome as well as experienced contributors.

## The 2026 program

Devcon has nine tracks:

- Core Protocol covers Ethereum research, its roadmap, consensus and staking, including the protocol's longer-term development.
- Privacy & Consent examines digital identity, self-sovereign identity and consent, alongside the effects of these systems on the communities using them.
- Security focuses on threat modeling, formal verification and operational security.
- Futures Worth Building considers coordination, public goods and open source, and how builders, communities and artists can influence technological choices.
- Users, Builders & Agents addresses wallets, account abstraction and user experience, with attention to security and privacy for people and agents using Ethereum.
- Rights, Freedoms & Governance uses case studies to examine human rights, DAOs and digital self-governance, including where these tools have failed.
- Applied Cryptography looks at practical uses of zero-knowledge proofs, multiparty computation and fully homomorphic encryption.
- Permissionless Networks covers peer-to-peer infrastructure, censorship resistance and connectivity under hostile network conditions.
- Open & Verifiable Stack examines open hardware, firmware and software, and how to verify the systems beneath an application.

Published session formats include five-minute lightning talks with two minutes for questions, 20-minute talks with five minutes for questions, 25-minute AMAs, fireside chats or roundtables, and hour-long hands-on workshops. Community hubs provide topic-focused educational spaces alongside coworking, art, music and interactive experiences. Announced speakers include Vitalik Buterin, Audrey Tang, Justin Drake, Roger Dingledine, Sandeep Nailwal, Hart Montgomery, Zachary Williamson and Fatemeh Fannizadeh. These tracks and formats describe the program; they are not a day-by-day session timetable.

## Tickets and attendance

General-admission tickets are sold in limited-quantity waves with purchase windows. The homepage currently lists US$499 when paying in ETH and US$999 in fiat, including 18% GST. Standard inclusions are four-day access, catering, hot drinks and event merchandise, with exceptions for some ticket types. Current availability and inclusions should be checked in the official ticket shop.

Community discounts require eligibility verification and a self-claimed discount code. They cover qualifying Indian residents and Ethereum or open-source contributors and participants. Review-based applications include student and Sanctuary Tech Builder tickets; approved applicants receive a voucher to purchase a ticket. The student route requires enrollment in an accredited degree program and relevant academic or community involvement. Short courses, bootcamps and online-only programs do not qualify. The FAQ lists October 23 as the final student application deadline, with responses by October 30.

General-admission tickets are transferable, can be purchased for someone else and allow entry with a QR code. Orders are limited to two tickets. Discounted tickets are non-transferable, must be claimed by the attendee and require ID at registration. Attendees under 16 must come with a parent or guardian who also holds a Devcon ticket.

The venue is accessible to attendees with disabilities. Sessions will be recorded and streamed on the organizer's YouTube channel. Devcon overlaps with Diwali travel, and the official travel guide includes accommodation and transport information.

Players register on the live game app and receive secret assignments:

- 24 hours of collaborative prototyping, firmware programming, and hardware integration.

description:
## Stark Space is coming to Mumbai!

Explore what's being built on Starknet, and meet the people building it.

Taking over one of Mumbai's most iconic restaurants, just a short walk from the main Devcon venue, Stark Space will be a place to plug in throughout the day.

What to expect

After programming, the space opens up into Stark Cafe. Grab a seat, start a conversation, or find a quiet corner to work - no agenda, no pressure. Then return on the evening of day 1 as Stark Space comes alive for a party.

The event is first-come-first-served with limited capacity - we recommend arriving early so you don't miss the morning session!

About Starknet

Starknet is a verifiable computer built to expand what products can do onchain. Built on proofs, it gives founders and developers more freedom to keep their products' defining logic onchain, with code written in Cairo and independent verification of execution powered by STARK proofs. Starknet operates as a validity rollup on Ethereum, which provides settlement. Its purpose is to enable a true peer-to-peer economy.

Talks, panels, fireside chats, workshops, and gamified exercises, organized around four tracks that run in parallel across the week rather than displacing one another:

Monad Foundation supports the growth and decentralization of the Monad ecosystem, a high-performance, EVM-compatible Layer 1 blockchain designed for speed, scalability, and low transaction costs. About ENS

Ethereum Name Service (ENS) is the decentralized naming protocol for Ethereum, making web3 more accessible through human-readable names. ENS enables users, developers, and applications to replace complex blockchain addresses with simple identities, while providing essential infrastructure for decentralized identity, payments, and interactions between humans and AI agents.

About STRATO

STRATO is an Ethereum-compatible blockchain platform designed to help enterprises build and deploy real-world blockchain applications. By combining blockchain infrastructure with enterprise-grade capabilities, STRATO enables organizations to develop secure, scalable solutions for tokenization, digital assets, and decentralized business processes.

About Consensys Diligence

Consensys Diligence is a leading blockchain security team specializing in smart contract audits, security assessments, and developer security tooling. name: Zcash Presents: FREE SOCIETY HACKATHON
description:
WebZero Events and Zcash host Free Society Hackathon at True Tramm Trunk BKC in Mumbai on 4 and 5 November 2026, during Devcon. The organizers are selecting 75 in-person builders to develop working products using Zcash, with an Agentic Commerce track from Bitrefill.

## Who can take part

Engineers, developers, product people, marketers and founders can apply, including people without a technical background or prior Zcash experience. The program starts with a tooling walkthrough, and mentors from Zcash projects provide workshops and one-to-one guidance throughout the build day.

Teams can have one to four people. Bring a team or find teammates at the venue. A project can enter both tracks if it meets each track's requirements.

## Tracks and prizes

The organizers advertise USD 5,000 in cash prizes. The published breakdown includes USD 4,800 in competition awards and USD 200 in conditional follow-up bonuses:

- The Zcash Privacy track awards USD 1,300 to the top project, two second prizes of USD 300 each and two third prizes of USD 200 each, totaling USD 2,300 across five projects.
- The Bitrefill Agentic Commerce track requires projects to use Bitrefill. It offers USD 1,000 for the most innovative project, USD 800 for second place, USD 600 for third and USD 100 for the best feedback, totaling USD 2,500.

Both USD 300 Privacy track winners are also named Zcash Ecosystem Prize winners. Each can earn a further USD 100 by agreeing on a milestone relevant to their submission and delivering it publicly. Those two milestone-dependent bonuses account for the remaining USD 200 in the advertised total.

## Schedule

All times are IST (Asia/Kolkata). Luma lists the event from 11:00 on Wednesday 4 November to 15:00 on Thursday 5 November 2026.

Wednesday 4 November is the hack day:

- 11:00: welcome and tooling walkthrough.
- 11:30: building begins, with workshops and mentors.
- Midnight at the end of hack day, listed as 00:00: submissions close.

Judges score every project overnight and select the teams that will demo on stage.

Thursday 5 November is demo day:

- 11:00: top teams announced.
- 12:00: demos and winners announced on stage.

## Food and facilities

Breakfast, lunch and dinner on hack day, plus an afterparty, are included. The venue provides hacking areas, fast internet and group seating. The organizers also advertise merchandise and describe the location as a short tuk-tuk ride from the main Devcon venue.

## After the hackathon

Winning teams will be paired with an ecosystem partner to agree, deliver and publicly share one small milestone within 30 days, with mentorship and support. The organizers say the same milestone-based follow-up is open to builders who do not win.

## Registration and venue

The Hacker Pass is free, but registration requires host approval. Applications are reviewed on a rolling basis for the 75 selected places. Participants must be in Mumbai in person on Wednesday 4 November; remote participation is not available.

The public venue is True Tramm Trunk BKC, G2-B, Ground Floor, Trade Centre Bkc, opposite MTNL, G Block, MMRDA Area, Bandra Kurla Complex, Bandra East, Mumbai, Maharashtra 400098, India.

name: Onchain Legal Summit :: Devcon India 2026
description:
Entity's third Onchain Legal Summit takes place during Devcon India on November 4, 2026, from 11:00 to 17:00 IST. The Legal & Governance Hub hosts this working summit for founders, lawyers, protocol designers and governance specialists examining the legal status of onchain entities, DAOs, AI agents and autonomous systems.

## Questions on the program

The announced subjects include:

- How DAO governance and compliance tools fit together, and how legal text can become computable contracts.
- Agent personhood, ERC-8004 and Know Your Agent, including the legal status of autonomous protocols and whether AI agents can hold voting rights in a DAO.
- Decentralized justice and AI arbitration for real-world disputes, and the use of onchain courts to resolve disagreements within DAOs.
- Legal recognition of onchain entities, whether they can operate across borders, and the compliance obligations involved in forming and running them.
- Registry infrastructure and the design of legal entities in Solidity and other programming environments.
- Liability for autonomous code and the use of onchain civil records for marriages, death certificates and notarization.
- How lawyers might express legal processes through APIs.

The India edition also examines online dispute resolution, digital public infrastructure and what national registries can learn from open registries. The organizer has published these themes but has not yet released a detailed agenda or session timetable. Speaker and partnership inquiries can be submitted through the form linked on the event page.

## Admission

Participation in the summit is free for Devcon 8 attendees. A separate valid Devcon ticket is required to enter the conference venue; registering on Luma or another external site does not provide Devcon admission. The event is for digital-asset founders and operators, general counsel, in-house compliance leads, and legal, regulatory and tax practitioners. Attendees are invited to contribute to the discussion.

The first part examines India's current legal and tax treatment of digital assets, including stablecoins, tokenization and FIU registration, with a focus on what these developments mean for businesses and their advisers.

name: Diyas : Near @Devcon
description:
ArQ and Abhiraj Mengade host Diyas: NEAR @Devcon in Mumbai on November 4, 2026, from 16:00 to 20:00 IST. The Diwali-themed gathering uses a team game to demonstrate NEAR cross-chain intents, with participants playing the roles of chains, swaps and confidential transactions.

Before arrival, NEAR AI uses each attendee's RSVP answers to create a physical persona card with a custom animated face and fragments of an intent. Participants find five other people and combine their fragments into a valid cross-chain instruction. The organizer's example is a confidential swap from NEAR to Solana.

The completed instruction goes to an Executor Booth, where an operator executes a US$1 to US$2 onchain micro-intent, with a testnet fallback, and prints the transaction hash. The group receives a Polaroid with the hash and a trusted execution environment (TEE) attestation on the back. That proof can be exchanged at the desk for Diwali merchandise offered as a game reward rather than for sale.

Attendees should complete the RSVP questionnaire and bring a phone and wallet handle. Solo participants can form groups at the door. Registration is free and requires host approval. The organizer describes a Mumbai workspace and rooftop setting; the public location listing identifies Mumbai without a specific street address.

name: ETHGlobal Mumbai 2026
description:
ETHGlobal Mumbai is an in-person hackathon from November 5 to 7, 2026, at Jio World Convention Centre, G Block, Bandra Kurla Complex, Bandra East, Mumbai. The program combines project building with technical mentorship, workshops and feedback sessions.

## Participation and project tracks

Applications are assessed individually. Hackers may work solo or in teams of up to five, but every member must be accepted and confirm their own place. The organizer's public registration data lists November 3 at 23:59 IST as the application deadline.

Accepted hackers confirm attendance with an ETH commitment stake. For an in-person event, its return requires official check-in, physical attendance and a project submission before the deadline; incomplete projects can still qualify for the stake return. ETHGlobal says returns normally take up to four weeks after the event. Applicants unable to stake because of financial constraints can contact the organizer about alternatives.

There are three ways to build:
- Classic / From Scratch: Project-specific code, designs and assets must begin during the hackathon. Public libraries and starter kits are allowed.
- Extend Open Source: Teams add substantive new work to an existing open-source codebase and identify what predates the event.
- Ship a Feature: Teams add new functionality to an existing product, including a private or commercial product. New parts submitted through the continuity tracks must remain open source, and partner-prize eligibility depends on the relevant track rules.

Teams must disclose pre-existing work in writing to ETHGlobal, document it in their submission and maintain a meaningful version-control history. AI tools are allowed with attribution: submissions should identify AI-assisted code or assets, retain meaningful human contributions and include the specifications, prompts and planning files used in spec-driven workflows.

Event Discord channels support announcements, team formation and mentorship. During the hackathon, mentors help with technical problems and project feedback. Participants under 18 need a separately submitted parent or guardian agreement. In-person attendees must check in and wear their event wristband throughout the event.

## Submission and judging

Projects are due through the Hacker Dashboard by November 7, 2026, at 09:00 IST; late submissions are not accepted. The submission includes a title, description and repository or equivalent project files, with new work distinguished from reused material. An optional demo video must be two to four minutes long and at least 720p. The organizer's video rules prohibit sped-up recordings, mobile-phone recordings, AI voiceovers and music-and-text-only explanations.

Teams can choose finalist judging plus partner prizes, or partner prizes only. They may select up to three partner prize programs; multiple tracks from one partner count as one program. Finalist judging requires a live presentation with four minutes for the demo and three minutes for questions. Judges consider technical difficulty, originality, practical completeness, usability and the project's distinctive qualities. The detailed judging guide says partners assess submitted materials and that booth presentations are optional for feedback. Partner winners are announced during the closing ceremony.

## Announced partner awards

The prize page lists World at US$12,500; ENS at US$10,000; 1inch at US$7,000; Definitive and Chainlink at US$5,000 each; and 0G, Uniswap Foundation, Arc, Hedera, Arkiv, Whitechain and Ethereum Foundation at US$15,000 each. These are announced partner prize allocations, with awards subject to each partner's requirements. Most partners have not yet published their detailed criteria.

1inch has published an Aqua application challenge for a DeFi position demonstrated through test scripts or a user interface. Its main US$5,000 pool is split into US$2,500, US$1,500 and US$1,000 awards. A separate continuity-track pool offers US$1,500 and US$500. Entries must use official Aqua/SwapVM contracts, demonstrate onchain token transfers in the final demo and provide a proper Git history; local forks and modified SwapVM redeployments are allowed. Projects using SwapVM receive additional judging consideration.

Definitive offers US$2,500 for a social trading application using Flash advanced orders and a separate US$2,500 continuity-track award for a creative Flash integration. Examples include copy trading, shared signals, agent-operated products, multi-agent workflows and voice or chat trading interfaces. Both challenges require a working trading flow through Flash API or Flash MCP advanced orders and onchain execution in the final demo. Entrants must also share a short product video on Discord and X, tagging @DefinitiveFi on X. The continuity award considers originality, technical creativity and the quality of the demonstration.

The [Mumbai submission guide](https://ethglobal.com/events/mumbai/info/details), [partner prize requirements](https://ethglobal.com/events/mumbai/prizes) and [ETHGlobal rules](https://ethglobal.com/rules) give the participation and award conditions.

description:
Aeternum organizes Unchained Summit India on November 5 and 6, 2026, at Courtyard by Marriott Mumbai International Airport in Andheri East. The conference is for institutional finance teams, investors, founders, developers, exchanges, policymakers and advisers working with digital assets and Web3.

## Two-day program

November 5 focuses on markets, finance and digital assets. Its announced topics are regulation and policy, tokenization and real-world assets, trading and markets, institutional adoption, stablecoins and payments, wealth and portfolio management, capital markets, and custody, liquidity and prime services.

November 6 focuses on Web3 infrastructure and emerging technology. Its announced subjects are AI and agentic systems, DeFi, blockchain scaling and infrastructure, security and digital trust, staking and network economics, consumer Web3 applications, emerging technologies, and interoperability and chain abstraction.

Across the program, the organizer's topic descriptions also cover India's digital-asset regulation, taxation and compliance; tokenized funds, securities and commodities; payment rails for settlement, remittances, treasury and commerce; machine payments and decentralized intelligence; and enterprise blockchain uses in settlement, trade, identity, data and tokenization.

## Announced speakers

The current India roster includes:
- S B Seker, Head of APAC at Binance; Praneeth Srikanti, Partner at Ethereal Ventures; and Prabal Banerjee, Co-Founder of Avail.
- Sanat Rao, Chief Investment Officer at Monarq Asset Management; Sumit Gupta, Co-Founder of CoinDCX; and Ashish Singhal, Co-Founder of CoinSwitch.
- Dilip Chenoy, Chairperson of Bharat Web3 Association; Roshan Prabhakar, Head of Product for India at Coinbase; Rajagopal Menon, Vice President at WazirX; and Saumya Saxena, Global Builder Lead at Base.

The organizer maintains the [full India speaker roster](https://unchainedsummit.com/india/speakers).

## Unchained Pitch Challenge

The Pitch Challenge takes place on November 5 within the summit. It accepts applications from Web3 startups under five years old, including protocols, DeFi projects, tokenized real-world asset projects and cross-chain tools. Teams may be at any funding stage. Applications should demonstrate product or technical strength, together with traction or an innovative roadmap.

Applicants submit a pitch deck for advisory-panel review. Only selected finalists are invited to pitch on stage, and winners are announced during the summit. The organizer describes press exposure and potential investor introductions as benefits; the page does not promise investment or a cash award.

The [pitch application page](https://unchainedsummit.com/india/pitch-competition/) contains conflicting cutoffs: its timeline says applications close October 25, with finalist selection on October 30, while its application callout says October 30. Applicants should confirm the cutoff with the organizer rather than rely on the later date.

Early-bird tickets are listed at US$149 for Standard and US$229 for VIP through October 26, 2026, with tax included. Standard includes conference sessions, networking and exhibition areas, lunch and coffee breaks. VIP adds access to the VIP and speaker lounge. The published last-chance prices are US$199 and US$299 respectively.

Only registered ticket holders may attend the summit and its networking events, and payment secures the booking. Registration may remain available until the first day if capacity allows. The FAQ specifies prior written authorization 90 days before the summit for ticket substitutions. The event is conducted in English without translation services, and the organizer encourages business-formal or smart-casual dress.

Personal audio/video recording is permitted. Publishing or transmitting recordings requires permission, with an exception for clips under one minute used in blogging or press coverage.

name: Frontier Of Intelligence Hackathon
description:
Frontier of Intelligence Hackathon brings developers, founders, researchers and designers working on AI, Web3 and autonomous systems to Mumbai from November 5, 2026, at 09:00 IST to November 6 at 17:00 IST. Hosted by Lakshmi, it offers mentorship in AI, cryptography and protocol design, alongside infrastructure partners for compute, LLM tooling and Web3 development. The organizer also describes routes to accelerator, grant and venture-capital opportunities.

## Technical tracks

- Autonomous AI Agents and Multi-Agent Systems: This track covers agents that coordinate onchain, execute financial or governance actions, interact with smart contracts and collaborate with other agents. It emphasizes agent economies, agent-to-agent commerce and onchain execution layers.
- Decentralized AI Infrastructure: Projects can address decentralized compute markets, verifiable inference, zero-knowledge machine learning (ZK-ML), distributed training or model marketplaces.
- Intelligence for Real-World Systems: Applications include healthcare AI infrastructure, climate coordination, financial intelligence, defense and cyber coordination, and autonomous supply chains.

## Announced awards

The US$5,000 grand prize is for the most impactful project across the tracks, assessed on technical depth, originality, real-world potential and scalability. Track winners are offered US$3,000 each. A separate US$2,000 Frontier Research Prize covers experimental, research-grade work such as ZK-ML, new coordination mechanisms, agent-to-agent economic systems and novel protocol design. These are competitive awards for selected projects; accelerator, grant and investor connections are opportunities rather than guaranteed funding for participants.

Registration is free and requires host approval. The exact Mumbai venue is private and available through registration.

name: Clear-Signing & Wallet Security @ DEVCON
description:
The ERC-8009 team is hosting an event dedicated to clear signing and ways to achieve it.

The existing and experimental solutions will be demonstrated using Ledger and Trezor devices.

Clear signing is a solution to Blind Signing, which is the single biggest security threat currently facing everyday Web3 users and protocol teams. It occurs when a hardware wallet cannot decode the transaction and present it in human language, so the end user approving the wallet transaction is left guessing whether the transaction is exactly what they intend to send. In many cases, unsuspecting users simply approve such transactions, accepting the risk.

Even though hardware wallets are commonly thought of as the ultimate security solution, they are still prone to attacks involving "blind signing". For example, that's exactly what happened to Bybit when the Safe code was modified and the hardware wallet couldn't provide a human-language explanation of the transaction (the famous $1.5B hack).

Join us during DEVCON Mumbai 2026 for a practical session exploring Clear-Signing solutions, amongst which ERC-8009 (Proxy Clear Signing) will be presented, with demos on real hardware devices.

name: Pr1me [London Series] - Exclusive Dinner for Web3 Finance
description:
Join us for the [London edition of the PR1ME Series, during Solana Breakpoint](https://solana.com/breakpoint) powered by the Onchain Finance Institute (OCF), [Solana Foundation](https://solana.org/), [Lukka](https://lukka.tech/) [and Breezing](https://breezing.io/).

This invite-only, community-driven gathering brings together leading minds in web3 accounting and finance.

This event is exclusively for finance professionals - CFOs, COOs, Controllers, Heads of Finance, or equivalent. We're unable to accept applications outside these roles.

Important: Only confirmed guests with a QR code will be allowed entry. Please note that walk-ins or unapproved registrations will not be possible.

## About Solana Foundation

[The Solana Foundation](https://solana.org/) is a non-profit organisation based in Zug, Switzerland, dedicated to the decentralisation, growth, and security of the Solana network. Solana is a proof-of-stake blockchain built for mass adoption. Fast, composable, green, and globally distributed.

## About Lukka

[Lukka](https://lukka.tech/) is the institutional data backbone for digital assets, transforming fragmented on-chain and off-chain activity into audit-ready intelligence. Trusted by global financial institutions, asset managers, custodians, exchanges, and regulators, Lukka delivers the trust, truth, and transparency needed to power pricing, valuation, compliance, risk management, accounting, and reporting across digital and tokenized assets.

## About Breezing

[Breezing](https://breezing.io/) is a crypto subledger built specifically for accounting professionals managing digital assets. It connects directly to blockchains, exchanges, and accounting systems like Xero and QuickBooks, eliminating the manual work of exporting CSVs and posting journal entries by hand.

[Used by 200+ businesses including ht.digital](https://ht.digital), BDO, ETH Global, Safe, and Dune.

SOC 2 certified and Swiss-made🇨🇭.

## About Onchain Finance Institute (OCF)

Onchain Finance Institute (OCF) (https://www.onchainfinanceinstitute.com/) is an education and community platform helping finance professionals build real-world onchain finance skills for accounting, treasury, and finance roles.

Join 150+ alumni and 400+ community members from organizations such as Solana Foundation, a16z, Ava Labs, Starknet, and more, upskilling with digital assets and transitioning into the future of onchain finance.

[Apply to join community platform](https://www.onchainfinanceinstitute.com/community).

> For sponsorship inquiries, you can reach out to hello@theaccountantquits.com

The University Blockchain Conference (UBC) - formerly the Midwest Blockchain Conference - is the leading access point connecting top university talent with the blockchain industry across the U.S. and beyond.

 Connecting Top Talent with Leading Companies

If you're a student or faculty member passionate about blockchain, this is your gateway. This November, connect with dozens of hiring companies, VCs eager to invest, and thought leaders excited to share knowledge with the next generation of builders.

The city's designers, artists, collectors, and creatives all in one room. If you've been onchain for years or you've never touched a crypto wallet in your life, you belong here.

This is the cultural exchange the city & crypto have been waiting for!

Attendance is free. RSVP required. Grab your pass above.

Happening at Web FLEA:

 Huge immersive layout for shopping and exploring

 Top DJs spinning all day

 White glove crypto wallet onboarding

 Every vendor accepts CRYPTO, card, and cash

 Food from the city's top restaurants

 Handpicked beverages flowing all day

 Curated digital art gallery

 NYC's top flea market vendors and brands

 Zines & print media

 Partner activations

 Tons of surprises and goodies throughout the day

Enjoy a full day of culture, community, and discovery, then join us for curated night vibes starting at 8pm.

Web Flea is Day 0 of ETHConf NYC. The conference takes over the Javits Center June 14 through 16, and the day before it starts, we set the tone for the week. Come in early, get your bearings in the city, and spend a Sunday with the people who actually make New York look and feel like New York.

The full lineup, vendors, and partners drop on the microsite: www.webflea.xyz

description:
ETHConf 2027 takes place at the Javits Center in New York City from June 14 to 16. The program brings Ethereum builders, founders, institutions, investors and policymakers together for main-stage discussions, technical sessions and product showcases.

Announced themes include stablecoins and payments, DeFi markets, Ethereum's protocol roadmap, scaling infrastructure, institutional adoption, and policy and governance. The site's past-speaker section describes earlier editions.

General passes cover conference stages and the exhibition. Pro passes add the networking app and lounge, catering and coworking; VIP passes add further hospitality and access. Sessions are to be recorded and made available to ticket holders within three weeks. Check the official pass comparison for current conditions.

name: Signal Week 2027
description:
The Bridge Between TradFi and Digital Assets. The Institutional Summit for Digital Assets. Paris, July 6-7, 2027.

## What it is

Signal Week is the summit for the institutional digital-assets sector, set in Paris. It succeeds seven years of Paris Blockchain Week as its elevation for the decade ahead: where Paris Blockchain Week built credibility as Europe's leading institutional digital asset conference, Signal Week positions it for the decade ahead.

## Audience

The organizer inherits an audience with more than 70% C-suite or investment decision-makers, 36,000-plus facilitated networking meetings, $50 trillion-plus in assets under management represented, and 389 government officials and policymakers. It is built for banking and financial services, asset management, enterprise, digital-asset native firms, traditional finance, infrastructure providers and family offices.

## Speakers

Past stages have hosted Changpeng Zhao (Binance), Jeremy Allaire (Circle), Lily Liu (Solana Foundation), Silvio Micali (Algorand), Charles Hoskinson, Joseph Lubin (ConsenSys), Tim Draper, Jan Van Eck (VanEck), Yoni Assia (eToro) and Arianna Simpson (a16z), alongside French ministers Anne Le Henanff, Clara Chappaz and Marina Ferrari. Featured faces for 2027 include Adam Back, Nikhil Sharma (BlackRock), Kara Kennedy (JP Morgan), Amy Oldenburg (Morgan Stanley), Ben Slavin (BNY), Christian Rau (Mastercard) and Daniel Seifert (Coinbase).

## Participation

Participants span digital-asset native builders, TradFi and fintech institutions deploying at scale, AI-for-finance providers and ecosystem partners. Founding partnerships for Signal Week 2027 are open.
